checks.question: Does the root separate generic identity/static definitions from music models and executable host instances?
checks.detail: Root exposes generic contracts and local modules. core uses workspace:* and is consumed by the separately exported music adapter. The contribution registry contains frozen definitions and implementation IDs; the controller keeps actual instances privately and takes build-injected factories. Catalog identity remains usable for non-music plugins.

checks.question: Are the generic root imports lightweight and implementations injected/lazy at discovery?
checks.detail: Static runtime import traversal reaches ten same-directory TypeScript files, with no external runtime import and no /music-sources, core, Vue, source implementation or codec edge. The behavioral probe confirms construction registers the descriptor without executing activate(); instances load only on activation. This is source-graph/test evidence, not a production build graph.

checks.question: Does registration cleanup retain owner identity and generation, while disable/late activation/unsubscribe preserve the projection contract?
checks.detail: B04-G01 fails: dispose() dereferences the caller-owned module.id after registration instead of the captured/frozen owner ID. Four supplemental controls pass: stale-generation/idempotent disposal, rejected registration atomicity, immediate projection withdrawal with deferred cleanup and unsubscribe, and pending activation invalidation with late-result suppression. These passing controller checks do not close the full enable/disable candidate.

checks.question: Is trusted ownership and authorization display distinguished from native granting authority?
checks.detail: Trust comes from host-injected owner sets/factories, with untrusted host implementations and trusted-only slots rejected by the registry. readPolicy is an injected read-only epoch/authorization projection. No native grant, storage, network or external-code installation operation is implemented by the generic root. Native enforcement and arbitrary external DTO validation are not accepted here.

The initial probe invocation had a cross-drive Vitest root setup error before any tests ran; the corrected invocation executes all five scenarios. findings.title: Cleanup reads mutable caller identity and can leave a contribution registered
findings.trigger: Register a mutable ModuleDescriptor with id one, change that original descriptor.id to renamed, and invoke the returned dispose(). ModuleDescriptor.id is mutable and registerBatch() intentionally copies/freezes the descriptor rather than freezing caller data.
findings.effect: The token lookup is performed under renamed, returns undefined, and exits without deleting the original one registration. one/view remains in the current snapshot and the owner generation remains reserved after disposal.
findings.impactLimit: Confirmed for the public registerBatch() API. The inspected production-facing ModuleController uses registry.replace(), so this finding does not establish a current product disable leak, executable resource leak or native authority bypass. Other application callers were not audited.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Capture the original owner ID before publication and use that immutable ID for disposal lookup/deletion while retaining the token check. Add a permanent regression for caller descriptor mutation and retain stale-generation/idempotent cleanup coverage in a separate fix task.

handoff: B04-generic-root-shared; baseline b87ac45bfb32b9cee89b77c2170b842a69f9f98f with unchanged plugin-center inputs. Only generic descriptor registration and its direct controller projection/disable chain were audited.

Ownership and static light-entry boundaries conform: ten same-directory runtime import nodes, no core/Vue/source/runtime dependency; host injects executable built-ins separately from frozen contribution definitions. Authorization is a read-only injected projection.

B04-G01 is an open P2 cleanup defect at contribution-registry.ts:76-78. Changing caller descriptor.id after registerBatch() makes dispose() miss the captured registration, leaving one/view in the snapshot. Current ModuleController uses replace(), so product disable/resource/native-authority failure is not established by this finding.

The retained package suite passes 51/51 in nine files and typecheck exits 0. The temporary five-scenario probe passes four controls and fails the identity-mutation cleanup assertion; corrected probe exit is 1. A preceding cross-drive Vitest configuration failure executed no tests and is recorded separately. Root import traversal exits 0. Logs/probe sources remain in the local temp path recorded above.
